summary: RNAS Yeovilton (HMS Heron) is a Royal Navy air station in Somerset, England, serving as the home of the Fleet Air Arm. It is one of the busiest military airfields in the UK and operates the Commando Helicopter Force, flying Wildcat and Merlin helicopters. The base is also famous for hosting the annual RNAS Yeovilton International Air Day, one of the largest airshows in Britain.
faqs:
Q: Is RNAS Yeovilton a public airport?
A: No, it is an active military air station operated by the Royal Navy and is not open to commercial passenger flights. Public access is limited to specific events and the on-site Fleet Air Arm Museum.

Q: What is the Fleet Air Arm Museum?
A: It is one of the world's largest aviation museums dedicated to naval aviation, featuring historic aircraft, interactive exhibits, and an aircraft carrier experience. The museum is located adjacent to the air station and is open to the public.

Q: When is the Yeovilton Air Day held?
A: The RNAS Yeovilton International Air Day typically takes place in July each year, featuring military and civilian aerobatic displays.

Q: Can civilians land aircraft at Yeovilton?
A: Civilian landings are generally not permitted as it is a military facility, though prior permission may be requested for specific purposes through the base authorities.
transport_tips: The nearest major road access is via the A303, with the airfield located just south of Yeovil. There is no dedicated public transport to the base, so visitors should plan to travel by car or arrange private transport. Taxis from Yeovil town centre are available but should be booked in advance due to limited availability in the rural area.
local_tip: If visiting for the Air Day, arrive early and use the dedicated shuttle bus from designated park-and-ride sites, as on-site parking fills up quickly and the queues at the main gate can be lengthy.
